highlights.rationale: Paper Theorem 4 verbatim: ∃ c>0 s.t. for every ε-standard pair (F,F') with ε<c, max_{i≤6} |M_i(F)-M_i(F')| ≥ ε^67. The Lean statement matches exactly — same existential constant c>0, same ε-standard hypothesis (EpsilonStandardPair F F' ε), and the conclusion ∃ i∈{1,..,6}, |M_i(F)-M_i(F')| ≥ ε^67 (max≥ encoded as ∃ i with that index in {1..6}).
highlights.prose: Theorem 4. There is a constant \(c>0\) such that, for any \( \)-standard \(F,F'\) and any \( <c\), \[ _ i 6 |M_i(F)-M_i(F')| ^ 67 \]

highlights.rationale: Qualitative ('six moments suffice') form of Theorem 4: if two nondegenerate two-Gaussian mixtures agree on all of their first six raw moments, they are equal up to component relabelling (MixtureRelabelEquiv). This is the identifiability statement that Theorem 4 is the robust quantitative version of (Section 3 intro: 'one of the first six raw moments will differ'); proved here as a direct corollary of theorem_4_polynomially_robust_identifiability. Linked to the Theorem 4 anchor at lower confidence because the paper states only the quantitative form as a numbered result, not this exact contrapositive.
highlights.prose: Theorem 4. There is a constant \(c>0\) such that, for any \( \)-standard \(F,F'\) and any \( <c\), \[ _ i 6 |M_i(F)-M_i(F')| ^ 67 \]

highlights.rationale: Paper Corollary 24: any centered Gaussian N(0,sigma^2,x) evaluated at |x| >= r is at most 1/(r*sqrt(2pi)). Lean: for r>0, mean=0 Gaussian, r<=|y| implies density y <= 1/(r*sqrt(2pi)) (uniform over sigma^2>0). Same statement.
Paper Fact 18 (first inequality): the L1 distance between N(mu,sigma^2) and the variance-scaled N(mu,sigma^2(1+delta)) is at most 10*delta. Lean states exactly this with 0 <= delta <= 1/2.

Lemma 29 (tail of central moment integrals): for σ²≤1, |μ|≤1/ε, the tail raw-moment integral ∫_{|x|≥2/ε} x^i N(μ,σ²,x) dx = O((1/ε^i)·exp(-1/(2ε²))). Lean states exactly this with an explicit absolute constant K_29 for i≤6.

Paper Lemma 5: for every eps-standard pair there is alpha with TV(F_alpha(F),F_alpha(F')) >= Omega(eps^4) and every deconvolved variance >= eps^12. The theorem states exactly this (K5*eps^4 TV gap, var >= eps^12, alpha < min varSq). Conf < 1 because the Lean version carries explicit prior-work measure-theoretic hypotheses; the existential structure and bounds match the paper statement.

highlights.rationale: Paper Lemma 6: deconvolution at alpha preserves low-order moment gaps up to a multiplicative factor, for two-component mixtures with all variances in [alpha,1]. Same statement (sum over i of moment-gap of deconvolved <= factor * sum of moment-gap of originals). NOTE: Lean uses the weaker multiplicative constant k*2^k*(k-1)!! in place of the paper's (k+1)!/floor(k/2)!; confidence lowered for the differing (looser) constant. Lean also requires alpha >= -1 (consistent with variances in [alpha,1]).
